- [EraPruning](https://docs.rs/type.EraPruningState.html)- State
- Tracks the current step of era pruning process for each era being lazily pruned.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasNominatorsSlashable.html)- Nominators - Slashable
- Per-era snapshot of whether nominators are slashable.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasRewardPoints.html)- Reward - Points
- Rewards for the last `Config::HistoryDepth`
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasStakersOverview.html)- Stakers - Overview
- Summary of validator exposure at a given era.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasStakersPaged.html)- Stakers - Paged
- Paginated exposure of a validator at given era.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasSumValidatorIncentiveWeight.html)- SumValidator - Incentive - Weight
- Sum of all validators’ incentive weights for the era.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasTotalStake.html)- Total - Stake
- The total amount staked for the last `Config::HistoryDepth`
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasValidatorIncentiveBudget.html)- Validator - Incentive - Budget
- The total validator incentive budget for the given era, snapshotted at era end.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasValidatorIncentiveWeight.html)- Validator - Incentive - Weight
- Individual validator incentive weight per era.
Each validator’s share of the incentive pot = `their_weight / sum_weight`.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasValidatorPrefs.html)- Validator - Prefs
- Exposure of validator at era with the preferences of validators.
- [Eras](https://docs.rs/type.ErasValidatorReward.html)- Validator - Reward
- The total staker reward budget for each era within `Config::HistoryDepth`
- [Force](https://docs.rs/type.ForceEra.html)- Era
- Mode of era forcing.
- [Hard](https://docs.rs/type.HardCapSelfStake.html)- CapSelf - Stake
- Hard cap on effective validator self-stake.
- [Last](https://docs.rs/type.LastValidatorEra.html)- Validator - Era
- Tracks the last era in which an account was active as a validator (included in the era’s exposure/snapshot).
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/type.Ledger.html)
- Map from all (unlocked) “controller” accounts to the info regarding the staking.
- [MaxCommission](https://docs.rs/type.MaxCommission.html)
- The maximum commission that validators can set.
- [MaxNominations](https://docs.rs/type.MaxNominationsOf.html)- Of
- Maximum number of nominations per nominator.
- [MaxNominators](https://docs.rs/type.MaxNominatorsCount.html)- Count
- The maximum nominator count before we stop allowing new validators to join.
- [MaxStaked](https://docs.rs/type.MaxStakedRewards.html)- Rewards
- Maximum staked rewards, i.e. the percentage of the era inflation that is used for stake rewards.
- [MaxValidators](https://docs.rs/type.MaxValidatorsCount.html)- Count
- The maximum validator count before we stop allowing new validators to join.
- [MaxWinners](https://docs.rs/type.MaxWinnersOf.html)- Of
- Alias for the maximum number of winners (aka. active validators), as defined in by this pallet’s config.
- [MaxWinners](https://docs.rs/type.MaxWinnersPerPageOf.html)- PerPage - Of
- Alias for the maximum number of winners per page, as expected by the election provider.
- [MinCommission](https://docs.rs/type.MinCommission.html)
- The minimum amount of commission that validators can set.
- [MinNominator](https://docs.rs/type.MinNominatorBond.html)- Bond
- The minimum active bond to become and maintain the role of a nominator.
- [MinValidator](https://docs.rs/type.MinValidatorBond.html)- Bond
- The minimum active bond to become and maintain the role of a validator.
- [Minimum](https://docs.rs/type.MinimumActiveStake.html)- Active - Stake
- The minimum active nominator stake of the last successful election.
- [Module](https://docs.rs/type.Module.html)- Deprecated
- Type alias to `Pallet`, to be used by`construct_runtime`.
- [Negative](https://docs.rs/type.NegativeImbalanceOf.html)- Imbalance - Of
- [Next](https://docs.rs/type.NextElectionPage.html)- Election - Page
- Keeps track of an ongoing multi-page election solution request.
- [Nominators](https://docs.rs/type.Nominators.html)
- The map from nominator stash key to their nomination preferences, namely the validators that they wish to support.
- [Offence](https://docs.rs/type.OffenceQueue.html)- Queue
- Stores reported offences in a queue until they are processed in subsequent blocks.
- [Offence](https://docs.rs/type.OffenceQueueEras.html)- Queue - Eras
- Tracks the eras that contain offences in `OffenceQueue`, sorted from**earliest to latest**.
- [Optimum](https://docs.rs/type.OptimumSelfStake.html)- Self - Stake
- Optimum self-stake threshold for validators.
- [Payee](https://docs.rs/type.Payee.html)
- Where the reward payment should be made. Keyed by stash.
- [Processing](https://docs.rs/type.ProcessingOffence.html)- Offence
- Tracks the currently processed offence record from the `OffenceQueue`.
- [Reward](https://docs.rs/type.RewardPoint.html)- Point
- Counter for the number of “reward” points earned by a given validator.
- [Self](https://docs.rs/type.SelfStakeSlopeFactor.html)- Stake - Slope - Factor
- Slope factor controlling the discouragement rate for self-stake between optimum and cap.
- [Slash](https://docs.rs/type.SlashRewardFraction.html)- Reward - Fraction
- The percentage of the slash that is distributed to reporters.
- [Unapplied](https://docs.rs/type.UnappliedSlashes.html)- Slashes
- All unapplied slashes that are queued for later.
- [Validator](https://docs.rs/type.ValidatorCount.html)- Count
- The ideal number of active validators.
- [Validator](https://docs.rs/type.ValidatorSlashInEra.html)- Slash - InEra
- All slashing events on validators, mapped by era to the highest slash proportion and slash value of the era.
- [Validators](https://docs.rs/type.Validators.html)
- The map from (wannabe) validator stash key to the preferences of that validator.
- [Virtual](https://docs.rs/type.VirtualStakers.html)- Stakers
- Stakers whose funds are managed by other pallets.
- [Voter](https://docs.rs/type.VoterSnapshotStatus.html)- Snapshot - Status
- Voter snapshot progress status.
- [__](https://docs.rs/type.__InherentHiddenInstance.html)- Inherent - Hidden - Instance
- Hidden instance generated to be internally used when module is used without instance.

# tytanic_filter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tytanic-filter/0.4.0/tytanic_filter/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#tytanic-filter)`tytanic-filter`

Filtering Tytanic test suites effectively.

This crates provides default implementations for the [ Filter](https://docs.rs/tytanic-core/0.4.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tytanic_core/filter/trait.Filter.html) trait, these
filters are used in the Tytanic CLI.

[§](https://docs.rs#exact-filter-sets)Exact Filter Sets

Exact filter sets can be turned into [ ExactFilter](https://docs.rs/exact/struct.ExactFilter.html), being an exact filter
means they emit errors when expected tests are missing once

[is called.](https://docs.rs/tytanic-core/0.4.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tytanic_core/filter/trait.FilterState.html#method.finish)

`FilterState::finish`[§](https://docs.rs#test-set-expressions)Test Set Expressions

Tests sets are expressions in a set-based DSL for filtering tests according to their identifiers, attributes, and annotations.

Test sets can be parsed and evaluated into an [ ExpressionFilter](https://docs.rs/test_set/struct.ExpressionFilter.html), unlike
explicit filters these are purely additive, i.e. missing tests do not cause
an error.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Combined](https://docs.rs/struct.CombinedFilter.html)- Filter
- A combined exact and test set expression filter.
- [Combined](https://docs.rs/struct.CombinedFilterState.html)- Filter - State
- Created by `Filter::state``CombinedFilter`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Returned by `FilterState::filter``FilterState::finish``CombinedFilterState`

# tytanic 0.4.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tytanic/0.4.0

# Tytanic

`tytanic` is a test runner for [Typst](https://typst.app) projects.
It helps you worry less about regressions and speeds up your development.

## Features

Out of the box `tytanic` supports the following features:

- compile and compare tests
- manage tests of various types
- manage and update reference documents when tests change
- filter tests effectively for concise test runs

## Documentation

To see how to get started with `tytanic`, check out the [book](https://typst-community.github.io/tytanic/index.html).

## Contribution

[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) contains some guidelines for contributing.

## Changelog

The changelog can be found [here](https://docs.rs/docs/CHANGELOG.md).

## License

Tytanic is dual-licensed under MIT or Apache 2.0 (`SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0`).

---

# axon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/axon-lang/2.34.0/axon/

## Expand description

AXON runtime library — exposes the full AXON runtime: compiler
frontend (re-exported from `axon-frontend`), handlers, runtime
primitives, ESK, HTTP/WebSocket servers, persistence, OTS pipelines.

Used by the `axon` binary and by integration tests.

[§](https://docs.rs#frontend-vs-runtime)Frontend vs runtime

§Fase 12.a — the compiler frontend (lexer, parser, AST, type checker,
IR generator, top-level checker, and the closed catalogs used by the
type checker) lives in the sibling crate `axon-frontend`, which has
zero runtime dependencies. This crate re-exports those modules
transparently so every existing caller (76 call sites across 26
files) keeps compiling without changes. The crate `axon-lsp`
consumes `axon-frontend` directly, skipping the runtime surface.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [advantage_](https://docs.rs/advantage_witness/index.html)- witness
- §Fase 69.a — the Advantage Witness: a transversal law
(`axon://logic/no_unwitnessed_advantage`). A primitive may not claim an advantage over a cheaper baseline without a machine-checkable witness on real data; the`AdvantageWitness`trait + closed metric catalog + verdict. §Fase 69.a — The Advantage Witness: a transversal Axon law.

# axon_emcp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/axon-emcp/0.20.0/axon_emcp/

## Expand description

`axon-emcp` — the official ℰMCP (Epistemic Model Context Protocol)
server for AXON, exposed as a library so integration tests under
`tests/` can drive the same `compiler_pipeline` and `knowledge`
surfaces the `main` binary uses at runtime.

The binary entrypoint lives in `src/main.rs`; everything callable
from outside the crate (tests, future embedders) goes through the
re-exports here. Keeping a hybrid bin+lib crate avoids duplicating
module bodies and ensures the in-binary code path and the
integration-test code path compile from the exact same source.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [compiler_](https://docs.rs/compiler_pipeline/index.html)- pipeline
- The lex → parse → type-check → IR-generate pipeline, projected through a single structured-diagnostic shape.
- [compose](https://docs.rs/compose/index.html)
- `axon.compose(intent)`— natural-language brief → typed scaffold.
- [knowledge](https://docs.rs/knowledge/index.html)
- The knowledge base catalogue.
- [otlp](https://docs.rs/otlp/index.html)
- §Fase 10 — OTLP/gRPC exporter follow-up to the §Fase 8 telemetry surface.
- [prompts](https://docs.rs/prompts/index.html)
- MCP prompts — parameterized prompt templates the host surfaces to the human user as named recipes (slash-commands, chat-menu entries, prompt pickers).
- [resources](https://docs.rs/resources/index.html)
- MCP resources the connected agent can read by URI.
- [scaffold](https://docs.rs/scaffold/index.html)
- `axon-emcp scaffold-primitive <name>`— stamp a markdown skeleton for one primitive’s documentation, with frontmatter pre-populated from the canonical- `PRIMITIVE_REGISTRY`
- [server](https://docs.rs/server/index.html)
- MCP protocol over stdio + JSON-RPC 2.0.
- [telemetry](https://docs.rs/telemetry/index.html)
- §Fase 8 — Telemetry surface, OTLP-grade in shape + privacy-first by construction.
- [tools](https://docs.rs/tools/index.html)
- MCP tools the connected agent can invoke.

---

# paste 1.0.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste/1.0.15

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.

## Pasting identifiers

Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to
form a single identifier.

```
use paste;
paste!
```
## More elaborate example

The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste invocation inside of a macro_rules macro.

```
use paste;
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!;
```
## Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an interpolated
segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`## Pasting documentation strings

Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #[doc ...] attribute are implicitly
concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.

```
use paste;
method_new!;  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
```

# paste - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste/1.0.15/target-redirect/paste/

## Expand description

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.

[§](https://docs.rs#pasting-identifiers)Pasting identifiers

Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`…`>]` are pasted
together to form a single identifier.

```
use paste::paste;
paste! {
    // Defines a const called `QRST`.
    const [<Q R S T>]: &str = "success!";
}
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(
        paste! { [<Q R S T>].len() },
        8,
    );
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#more-elaborate-example)More elaborate example

The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste invocation inside of a macro_rules macro.

```
use paste::paste;
macro_rules! make_a_struct_and_getters {
    ($name:ident { $($field:ident),* }) => {
        // Define a struct. This expands to:
        //
        //     pub struct S {
        //         a: String,
        //         b: String,
        //         c: String,
        //     }
        pub struct $name {
            $(
                $field: String,
            )*
        }
        // Build an impl block with getters. This expands to:
        //
        //     impl S {
        //         pub fn get_a(&self) -> &str { &self.a }
        //         pub fn get_b(&self) -> &str { &self.b }
        //         pub fn get_c(&self) -> &str { &self.c }
        //     }
        paste! {
            impl $name {
                $(
                    pub fn [<get_ $field>](&self) -> &str {
                        &self.$field
                    }
                )*
            }
        }
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!(S { a, b, c });
fn call_some_getters(s: &S) -> bool {
    s.get_a() == s.get_b() && s.get_c().is_empty()
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#case-conversion)Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an
interpolated segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For
example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked
with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`[§](https://docs.rs#pasting-documentation-strings)Pasting documentation strings

Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #[doc …] attribute are
implicitly concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.

```
use paste::paste;
macro_rules! method_new {
    ($ret:ident) => {
        paste! {
            #[doc = "Create a new `" $ret "` object."]
            pub fn new() -> $ret { todo!() }
        }
    };
}
pub struct Paste {}
method_new!(Paste);  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
```

[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! [`concat_idents!`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro,
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! including using pasted identifiers to define new items.
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! <br>
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! # Pasting identifiers
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! together to form a single identifier.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ```
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! use paste::paste;
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! paste! {
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!     // Defines a const called `QRST`.
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!     const [<Q R S T>]: &str = "success!";
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! }
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! fn main() {
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!     assert_eq!(
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!         paste! { [<Q R S T>].len() },
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!         8,
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!     );
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! }
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! ```
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! <br><br>
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! # More elaborate example
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! paste invocation inside of a macro\_rules macro.
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! ```
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! use paste::paste;
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! macro_rules! make_a_struct_and_getters {
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!     ($name:ident { $($field:ident),* }) => {
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!         // Define a struct. This expands to:
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!         //
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!         //     pub struct S {
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!         //         a: String,
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!         //         b: String,
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!         //         c: String,
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!         //     }
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!         pub struct $name {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!             $(
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!                 $field: String,
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!             )*
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!         }
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!         // Build an impl block with getters. This expands to:
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!         //
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!         //     impl S {
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!         //         pub fn get_a(&self) -> &str { &self.a }
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!         //         pub fn get_b(&self) -> &str { &self.b }
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!         //         pub fn get_c(&self) -> &str { &self.c }
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!         //     }
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!         paste! {
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!             impl $name {
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//!                 $(
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!                     pub fn [<get_ $field>](&self) -> &str {
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!                         &self.$field
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!                     }
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!                 )*
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!             }
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!         }
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!     }
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! }
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! make_a_struct_and_getters!(S { a, b, c });
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! fn call_some_getters(s: &S) -> bool {
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!     s.get_a() == s.get_b() && s.get_c().is_empty()
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! }
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! #
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! # fn main() {}
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! ```
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! <br><br>
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! # Case conversion
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//!
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! interpolated segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! with $reg=`Bc`.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//!
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake\_case.
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! Use `$var:camel` to convert snake\_case to CamelCase.
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING\_CASE.
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//!
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [`str::to_lowercase`] and
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! [`str::to_uppercase`].
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//!
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! [`str::to_lowercase`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! [`str::to_uppercase`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//!
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! <br>
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//!
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//! # Pasting documentation strings
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//!
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//! Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #\[doc ...\] attribute are
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//! implicitly concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! ```
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//! use paste::paste;
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//!
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//! macro_rules! method_new {
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!     ($ret:ident) => {
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!         paste! {
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!             #[doc = "Create a new `" $ret "` object."]
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//!             pub fn new() -> $ret { todo!() }
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!         }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//!     };
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//! }
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! pub struct Paste {}
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! method_new!(Paste);  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! ```
[139](https://docs.rs#139)
[140](https://docs.rs#140)#![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/paste/1.0.15")]
[141](https://docs.rs#141)#![allow(

[144](https://docs.rs#144)    clippy::match_same_arms,
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    clippy::module_name_repetitions,
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    clippy::needless_doctest_main,
[147](https://docs.rs#147)    clippy::too_many_lines
[148](https://docs.rs#148))]

[195](https://docs.rs#195)
[196](https://docs.rs#196)fn expand(
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    input: [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html),
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    contains_paste: &mut [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    flatten_single_interpolation: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
[200](https://docs.rs#200)) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#4)<[TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)> {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    let mut expanded = [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)::[new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html#method.new)();
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    let mut lookbehind = Lookbehind::[Other](https://docs.rs#293);
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    let mut prev_none_group = [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)::<[Group](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html)>;
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    let mut tokens = [input](https://docs.rs#197).[into_iter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html#tymethod.into_iter)().[peekable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.peekable)();
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    loop {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)        let token = [tokens](https://docs.rs#204).[next](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#tymethod.next)();
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(group) = [prev_none_group](https://docs.rs#203).[take](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.take)() {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)            if match (&[token](https://docs.rs#206), [tokens](https://docs.rs#204).[peek](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/adapters/peekable/struct.Peekable.html#method.peek)()) {
[209](https://docs.rs#209)                ([Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(TokenTree::[Punct](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Punct)(fst)), [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(TokenTree::[Punct](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Punct)(snd))) => {
[210](https://docs.rs#210)                    [fst](https://docs.rs#209).[as_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.as_char)() == ':' && [snd](https://docs.rs#209).[as_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.as_char)() == ':' && [fst](https://docs.rs#209).[spacing](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.spacing)() == Spacing::[Joint](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.Spacing.html#variant.Joint)
[211](https://docs.rs#211)                }
[212](https://docs.rs#212)                _ => false,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)            } {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)                [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)([group](https://docs.rs#207).[stream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.stream)());
[215](https://docs.rs#215)                *[contains_paste](https://docs.rs#198) = true;
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            } else {
[217](https://docs.rs#217)                [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)(iter::[once](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/sources/once/fn.once.html)(TokenTree::[Group](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Group)([group](https://docs.rs#207))));
[218](https://docs.rs#218)            }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)        }
[220](https://docs.rs#220)        match [token](https://docs.rs#206) {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(TokenTree::[Group](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Group)(group)) => {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)                let delimiter = [group](https://docs.rs#221).[delimiter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.delimiter)();
[223](https://docs.rs#223)                let content = [group](https://docs.rs#221).[stream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.stream)();
[224](https://docs.rs#224)                let span = [group](https://docs.rs#221).[span](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.span)();
[225](https://docs.rs#225)                if [delimiter](https://docs.rs#222) == Delimiter::[Bracket](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.Delimiter.html#variant.Bracket) && [is_paste_operation](https://docs.rs#334-352)(&[content](https://docs.rs#223)) {
[226](https://docs.rs#226)                    let segments = parse_bracket_as_segments(content, span)?;
[227](https://docs.rs#227)                    let pasted = segment::paste(&segments)?;
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                    let tokens = pasted_to_tokens(pasted, span)?;
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                    [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)([tokens](https://docs.rs#228));
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                    *[contains_paste](https://docs.rs#198) = true;
[231](https://docs.rs#231)                } else if [flatten_single_interpolation](https://docs.rs#199)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)                    && [delimiter](https://docs.rs#222) == Delimiter::[None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.Delimiter.html#variant.None)
[233](https://docs.rs#233)                    && [is_single_interpolation_group](https://docs.rs#297-332)(&[content](https://docs.rs#223))
[234](https://docs.rs#234)                {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)                    [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)([content](https://docs.rs#223));
[236](https://docs.rs#236)                    *[contains_paste](https://docs.rs#198) = true;
[237](https://docs.rs#237)                } else {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)                    let mut group_contains_paste = false;
[239](https://docs.rs#239)                    let is_attribute = [delimiter](https://docs.rs#222) == Delimiter::[Bracket](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.Delimiter.html#variant.Bracket)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)                        && ([lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) == Lookbehind::[Pound](https://docs.rs#291) || [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) == Lookbehind::[PoundBang](https://docs.rs#292));
[241](https://docs.rs#241)                    let mut nested = expand(
[242](https://docs.rs#242)                        content,
[243](https://docs.rs#243)                        &mut group_contains_paste,
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                        flatten_single_interpolation && !is_attribute,
[245](https://docs.rs#245)                    )?;
[246](https://docs.rs#246)                    if [is_attribute](https://docs.rs#239) {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)                        [nested](https://docs.rs#241) = expand_attr(nested, span, &mut group_contains_paste)?;
[248](https://docs.rs#248)                    }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)                    let group = if [group_contains_paste](https://docs.rs#238) {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)                        let mut group = [Group](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html)::[new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.new)([delimiter](https://docs.rs#222), [nested](https://docs.rs#241));
[251](https://docs.rs#251)                        [group](https://docs.rs#250).[set_span](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.set_span)([span](https://docs.rs#224));
[252](https://docs.rs#252)                        *[contains_paste](https://docs.rs#198) = true;
[253](https://docs.rs#253)                        [group](https://docs.rs#250)
[254](https://docs.rs#254)                    } else {
[255](https://docs.rs#255)                        [group](https://docs.rs#221).[clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone)()
[256](https://docs.rs#256)                    };
[257](https://docs.rs#257)                    if [delimiter](https://docs.rs#222) != Delimiter::[None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.Delimiter.html#variant.None) {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)                        [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)(iter::[once](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/sources/once/fn.once.html)(TokenTree::[Group](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Group)([group](https://docs.rs#249))));
[259](https://docs.rs#259)                    } else if [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) == Lookbehind::[DoubleColon](https://docs.rs#290) {
[260](https://docs.rs#260)                        [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)([group](https://docs.rs#249).[stream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Group.html#method.stream)());
[261](https://docs.rs#261)                        *[contains_paste](https://docs.rs#198) = true;
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                    } else {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)                        [prev_none_group](https://docs.rs#203) = [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)([group](https://docs.rs#249));
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                    }
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                }
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) = Lookbehind::[Other](https://docs.rs#293);
[267](https://docs.rs#267)            }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)            [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(TokenTree::[Punct](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Punct)(punct)) => {
[269](https://docs.rs#269)                [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) = match [punct](https://docs.rs#268).[as_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.as_char)() {
[270](https://docs.rs#270)                    ':' if [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) == Lookbehind::[JointColon](https://docs.rs#289) => Lookbehind::[DoubleColon](https://docs.rs#290),
[271](https://docs.rs#271)                    ':' if [punct](https://docs.rs#268).[spacing](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.spacing)() == Spacing::[Joint](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.Spacing.html#variant.Joint) => Lookbehind::[JointColon](https://docs.rs#289),
[272](https://docs.rs#272)                    '#' => Lookbehind::[Pound](https://docs.rs#291),
[273](https://docs.rs#273)                    '!' if [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) == Lookbehind::[Pound](https://docs.rs#291) => Lookbehind::[PoundBang](https://docs.rs#292),
[274](https://docs.rs#274)                    _ => Lookbehind::[Other](https://docs.rs#293),
[275](https://docs.rs#275)                };
[276](https://docs.rs#276)                [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)(iter::[once](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/sources/once/fn.once.html)(TokenTree::[Punct](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Punct)([punct](https://docs.rs#268))));
[277](https://docs.rs#277)            }
[278](https://docs.rs#278)            [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(other) => {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                [lookbehind](https://docs.rs#202) = Lookbehind::[Other](https://docs.rs#293);
[280](https://docs.rs#280)                [expanded](https://docs.rs#201).[extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html#tymethod.extend)(iter::[once](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/sources/once/fn.once.html)([other](https://docs.rs#278)));
[281](https://docs.rs#281)            }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)            [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) => return [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)([expanded](https://docs.rs#201)),
[283](https://docs.rs#283)        }
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    }
[285](https://docs.rs#285)}
[286](https://docs.rs#286)
[287](https://docs.rs#287)#[derive([PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.PartialEq.html))]
[288](https://docs.rs#288)enum [Lookbehind](https://docs.rs#288-294) {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    JointColon,
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    DoubleColon,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    Pound,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    PoundBang,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    Other,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)}

[296](https://docs.rs#296)// https://github.com/dtolnay/paste/issues/26
[297](https://docs.rs#297)fn is_single_interpolation_group(input: &[TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    #[derive([PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.PartialEq.html))]
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    enum [State](https://docs.rs#299-307) {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)        Init,
[301](https://docs.rs#301)        Ident,
[302](https://docs.rs#302)        Literal,
[303](https://docs.rs#303)        Apostrophe,
[304](https://docs.rs#304)        Lifetime,
[305](https://docs.rs#305)        Colon1,
[306](https://docs.rs#306)        Colon2,
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    }
[308](https://docs.rs#308)
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    let mut state = State::[Init](https://docs.rs#300);
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    for tt in input.clone() {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)        state = match (state, &tt) {
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            (State::Init, TokenTree::Ident(_)) => State::Ident,
[313](https://docs.rs#313)            (State::Init, TokenTree::Literal(_)) => State::Literal,
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            (State::Init, TokenTree::Punct(punct)) if punct.as_char() == '\'' => State::Apostrophe,
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            (State::Apostrophe, TokenTree::Ident(_)) => State::Lifetime,
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            (State::Ident, TokenTree::Punct(punct))
[317](https://docs.rs#317)                if punct.as_char() == ':' && punct.spacing() == Spacing::Joint =>
[318](https://docs.rs#318)            {
[319](https://docs.rs#319)                State::Colon1
[320](https://docs.rs#320)            }
[321](https://docs.rs#321)            (State::Colon1, TokenTree::Punct(punct))
[322](https://docs.rs#322)                if punct.as_char() == ':' && punct.spacing() == Spacing::Alone =>
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            {
[324](https://docs.rs#324)                State::Colon2
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            }
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            (State::Colon2, TokenTree::Ident(_)) => State::Ident,
[327](https://docs.rs#327)            _ => return false,
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        };
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    }
[330](https://docs.rs#330)
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    [state](https://docs.rs#309) == State::[Ident](https://docs.rs#301) || [state](https://docs.rs#309) == State::[Literal](https://docs.rs#302) || [state](https://docs.rs#309) == State::[Lifetime](https://docs.rs#304)
[332](https://docs.rs#332)}

[334](https://docs.rs#334)fn is_paste_operation(input: &[TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    let mut tokens = [input](https://docs.rs#334).[clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone)().[into_iter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html#tymethod.into_iter)();

[339](https://docs.rs#339)        _ => return false,
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    }
[341](https://docs.rs#341)
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    let mut has_token = false;
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    loop {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        match &[tokens](https://docs.rs#335).[next](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#tymethod.next)() {
[345](https://docs.rs#345)            [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(TokenTree::[Punct](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Punct)(punct)) if [punct](https://docs.rs#345).[as_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.as_char)() == '>' => {

[347](https://docs.rs#347)            }
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(_) => [has_token](https://docs.rs#342) = true,
[349](https://docs.rs#349)            [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) => return false,
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        }

[364](https://docs.rs#364)
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    match &[tokens](https://docs.rs#355).[next](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#tymethod.next)() {
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(TokenTree::[Punct](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#variant.Punct)(punct)) if [punct](https://docs.rs#366).[as_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Punct.html#method.as_char)() == '>' => {}
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(wrong) => return [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)([Error](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#6-10)::[new](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#13-15)([wrong](https://docs.rs#367).[span](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#method.span)(), "expected `>`")),
[368](https://docs.rs#368)        [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) => return [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)([Error](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#6-10)::[new](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#13-15)([scope](https://docs.rs#354), "expected `[< ... >]`")),
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    }
[370](https://docs.rs#370)
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(unexpected) = [tokens](https://docs.rs#355).[next](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#tymethod.next)() {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)        return [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)([Error](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#6-10)::[new](https://docs.rs/error.rs.html#13-15)(
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            [unexpected](https://docs.rs#371).[span](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/enum.TokenTree.html#method.span)(),
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            "unexpected input, expected `[< ... >]`",
[375](https://docs.rs#375)        ));
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    }
[377](https://docs.rs#377)
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    for segment in &mut segments {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        if let Segment::String(string) = segment {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            if string.value.starts_with("'\\u{") {
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                let hex = &string.value[4..string.value.len() - 2];
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                if let Ok(unsigned) = u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16) {
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                    if let Some(ch) = char::from_u32(unsigned) {
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                        string.value.clear();
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                        string.value.push(ch);
[386](https://docs.rs#386)                        continue;
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                    }
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                }
[389](https://docs.rs#389)            }
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            if string.value.contains(&['#', '\\', '.', '+'][..])
[391](https://docs.rs#391)                || string.value.starts_with("b'")
[392](https://docs.rs#392)                || string.value.starts_with("b\"")
[393](https://docs.rs#393)                || string.value.starts_with("br\"")
[394](https://docs.rs#394)            {
[395](https://docs.rs#395)                return Err(Error::new(string.span, "unsupported literal"));
[396](https://docs.rs#396)            }
[397](https://docs.rs#397)            let mut range = 0..string.value.len();
[398](https://docs.rs#398)            if string.value.starts_with("r\"") {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)                range.start += 2;
[400](https://docs.rs#400)                range.end -= 1;
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            } else if string.value.starts_with(&['"', '\''][..]) {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                range.start += 1;
[403](https://docs.rs#403)                range.end -= 1;
[404](https://docs.rs#404)            }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)            string.value = string.value[range].replace('-', "_");
[406](https://docs.rs#406)        }
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    }

# paste - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/paste/latest/paste/

## Expand description

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.

[§](https://docs.rs#pasting-identifiers)Pasting identifiers

Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`…`>]` are pasted
together to form a single identifier.

```
use paste::paste;
paste! {
    // Defines a const called `QRST`.
    const [<Q R S T>]: &str = "success!";
}
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(
        paste! { [<Q R S T>].len() },
        8,
    );
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#more-elaborate-example)More elaborate example

The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste invocation inside of a macro_rules macro.

```
use paste::paste;
macro_rules! make_a_struct_and_getters {
    ($name:ident { $($field:ident),* }) => {
        // Define a struct. This expands to:
        //
        //     pub struct S {
        //         a: String,
        //         b: String,
        //         c: String,
        //     }
        pub struct $name {
            $(
                $field: String,
            )*
        }
        // Build an impl block with getters. This expands to:
        //
        //     impl S {
        //         pub fn get_a(&self) -> &str { &self.a }
        //         pub fn get_b(&self) -> &str { &self.b }
        //         pub fn get_c(&self) -> &str { &self.c }
        //     }
        paste! {
            impl $name {
                $(
                    pub fn [<get_ $field>](&self) -> &str {
                        &self.$field
                    }
                )*
            }
        }
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!(S { a, b, c });
fn call_some_getters(s: &S) -> bool {
    s.get_a() == s.get_b() && s.get_c().is_empty()
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#case-conversion)Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an
interpolated segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For
example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked
with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`[§](https://docs.rs#pasting-documentation-strings)Pasting documentation strings

Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #[doc …] attribute are
implicitly concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.

```
use paste::paste;
macro_rules! method_new {
    ($ret:ident) => {
        paste! {
            #[doc = "Create a new `" $ret "` object."]
            pub fn new() -> $ret { todo!() }
        }
    };
}
pub struct Paste {}
method_new!(Paste);  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
```

# paste 1.0.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# rustversion 1.0.22 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rustversion/^1.0

# Compiler version cfg

This crate provides macros for conditional compilation according to rustc
compiler version, analogous to [ #[cfg(...)]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg-attribute) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg_attr-attribute)

`#[cfg_attr(...)]````
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Selectors

-
`#[rustversion::stable]`— True on any stable compiler.
-
`#[rustversion::stable(1.34)]`— True on exactly the specified stable compiler.
-
`#[rustversion::beta]`— True on any beta compiler.
-
`#[rustversion::nightly]`— True on any nightly compiler or dev build.
-
`#[rustversion::nightly(2025-01-01)]`— True on exactly one nightly.
-
`#[rustversion::since(1.34)]`— True on that stable release and any later compiler, including beta and nightly.
-
`#[rustversion::since(2025-01-01)]`— True on that nightly and all newer ones.
-
`#[rustversion::before(`version or date`)]`— Negative of*#[rustversion::since(...)]*.
-
`#[rustversion::not(`selector`)]`— Negative of any selector; for example*#[rustversion::not(nightly)]*.
-
`#[rustversion::any(`selectors...`)]`— True if any of the comma-separated selectors is true; for example*#[rustversion::any(stable, beta)]*.
-
`#[rustversion::all(`selectors...`)]`— True if all of the comma-separated selectors are true; for example*#[rustversion::all(since(1.31), before(1.34))]*.
-
`#[rustversion::attr(`selector`,`attribute`)]`— For conditional inclusion of attributes; analogous to`cfg_attr`.
-
`rustversion::cfg!(`selector`)`— An expression form of any of the above attributes; for example*if rustversion::cfg!(any(stable, beta)) { ... }*.

## Use cases

Providing additional trait impls as types are stabilized in the standard library
without breaking compatibility with older compilers; in this case Pin<P>
stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2019/02/28/Rust-1.33.0.html#pinning):

```
use Pin;
```
Similar but for language features; the ability to control alignment greater than
1 of packed structs was stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/RELEASES.md#version-1330-2019-02-28).

```
;
```
Augmenting code with `const` as const impls are stabilized in the standard
library. This use of `const` as an attribute is recognized as a special case by
the rustversion::attr macro.

```
use Duration;
```
Emitting Cargo cfg directives from a build script. Note that this requires
listing `rustversion` under `[build-dependencies]` in Cargo.toml, not
`[dependencies]`.

```
// build.rs
```
```
// src/lib.rs
extern crate alloc;
```

# trybuild 1.0.117 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/trybuild/^1.0.49

# Trybuild

Trybuild is a test harness for invoking rustc on a set of test cases and asserting that any resulting error messages are the ones intended.

Such tests are commonly useful for testing error reporting involving procedural macros. We would write test cases triggering either errors detected by the macro or errors detected by the Rust compiler in the resulting expanded code, and compare against the expected errors to ensure that they remain user-friendly.

This style of testing is sometimes called *ui tests* because they test aspects
of the user's interaction with a library outside of what would be covered by
ordinary API tests.

Nothing here is specific to macros; trybuild would work equally well for testing misuse of non-macro APIs.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Compile-fail tests

A minimal trybuild setup looks like this:

```
```
The test can be run with `cargo test`. It will individually compile each of the
source files matching the glob pattern, expect them to fail to compile, and
assert that the compiler's error message matches an adjacently named **.stderr*
file containing the expected output (same file name as the test except with a
different extension). If it matches, the test case is considered to succeed.

Dependencies listed under `[dev-dependencies]` in the project's Cargo.toml are
accessible from within the test cases.

Failing tests display the expected vs actual compiler output inline.

A compile_fail test that fails to fail to compile is also a failure.

To test just one source file, use:

```
cargo test -- ui trybuild=example.rs
```
where `ui` is the name of the `#[test]` function that invokes `trybuild`, and
`example.rs` is the name of the file to test.

## Pass tests

The same test harness is able to run tests that are expected to pass, too.
Ordinarily you would just have Cargo run such tests directly, but being able to
combine modes like this could be useful for workshops in which participants work
through test cases enabling one at a time. Trybuild was originally developed for
my [procedural macros workshop at Rust Latam](https://github.com/dtolnay/proc-macro-workshop).

```
```
Pass tests are considered to succeed if they compile successfully and have a
`main` function that does not panic when the compiled binary is executed.

## Details

That's the entire API.

## Workflow

There are two ways to update the **.stderr* files as you iterate on your test
cases or your library; handwriting them is not recommended.

First, if a test case is being run as compile_fail but a corresponding
**.stderr* file does not exist, the test runner will save the actual compiler
output with the right filename into a directory called *wip* within the
directory containing Cargo.toml. So you can update these files by deleting them,
running `cargo test`, and moving all the files from *wip* into your testcase
directory.

Alternatively, run `cargo test` with the environment variable
`TRYBUILD=overwrite` to skip the *wip* directory and write all compiler output
directly in place. You'll want to check `git diff` afterward to be sure the
compiler's output is what you had in mind.

## What to test

When it comes to compile-fail tests, write tests for anything for which you care to find out when there are changes in the user-facing compiler output. As a negative example, please don't write compile-fail tests simply calling all of your public APIs with arguments of the wrong type; there would be no benefit.

A common use would be for testing specific targeted error messages emitted by a
procedural macro. For example the derive macro from the [ ref-cast](https://github.com/dtolnay/ref-cast) crate is
required to be placed on a type that has either

`#[repr(C)]` or
`#[repr(transparent)]` in order for the expansion to be free of undefined
behavior, which it enforces at compile time:```
error: RefCast trait requires #[repr(C)] or #[repr(transparent)]
 --> $DIR/missing-repr.rs:3:10
  |
3 | #[derive(RefCast)]
  |          ^^^^^^^
```
Macros that consume helper attributes will want to check that unrecognized content within those attributes is properly indicated to the caller. Is the error message correctly placed under the erroneous tokens, not on a useless call_site span?

```
error: unknown serde field attribute `qqq`
 --> $DIR/unknown-attribute.rs:5:13
  |
5 |     #[serde(qqq = "...")]
  |             ^^^
```
Declarative macros can benefit from compile-fail tests too. The [ json!](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0/serde_json/macro.json.html) macro
from serde_json is just a great big macro_rules macro but makes an effort to
have error messages from broken JSON in the input always appear on the most
appropriate token:

```
error: no rules expected the token `,`
 --> $DIR/double-comma.rs:4:38
  |
4 |     println!("{}", json!({ "k": null,, }));
  |                                      ^ no rules expected this token in macro call
```
Sometimes we may have a macro that expands successfully but we count on it to
trigger particular compiler errors at some point beyond macro expansion. For
example the [ readonly](https://github.com/dtolnay/readonly) crate introduces struct fields that are public but
readable only, even if the caller has a &mut reference to the surrounding
struct. If someone writes to a readonly field, we need to be sure that it
wouldn't compile:

```
error[E0594]: cannot assign to data in a `&` reference
  --> $DIR/write-a-readonly.rs:17:26
   |
17 |     println!("{}", s.n); s.n += 1;
   |                          ^^^^^^^^ cannot assign
```
In all of these cases, the compiler's output can change because our crate or one of our dependencies broke something, or as a consequence of changes in the Rust compiler. Both are good reasons to have well conceived compile-fail tests. If we refactor and mistakenly cause an error that used to be correct to now no longer be emitted or be emitted in the wrong place, that is important for a test suite to catch. If the compiler changes something that makes error messages that we care about substantially worse, it is also important to catch and report as a compiler issue.

## Troubleshooting

The Rust compiler's diagnostic output can vary as a function of whether the
`rust-src` Rustup component is installed. The compiler will render source
snippets from the standard library if the standard library source is available
locally, and will simply omit snippets if not. This can account for differences
between CI and local development.

If you have compile_fail tests pertaining to standard library traits or types, you can ensure a consistent environment by adding a rust-toolchain.toml file with the following content.

```
[]
 = ["rust-src"]
```

---

# paste 1.0.14 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste/1.0.14

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.

## Pasting identifiers

Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to
form a single identifier.

```
use paste;
paste!
```
## More elaborate example

The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste invocation inside of a macro_rules macro.

```
use paste;
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!;
```
## Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an interpolated
segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`## Pasting documentation strings

Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #[doc ...] attribute are implicitly
concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.

```
use paste;
method_new!;  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
```

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.

## Pasting identifiers

Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to
form a single identifier.

```
use paste;
paste!
```
## More elaborate example

The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste invocation inside of a macro_rules macro.

```
use paste;
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!;
```
## Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an interpolated
segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`## Pasting documentation strings

Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #[doc ...] attribute are implicitly
concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.

```
use paste;
method_new!;  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
```

---

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```

This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
This approach works with any stable or nightly Rust compiler 1.30+.

## Pasting identifiers

There are two entry points, `paste::expr!` for macros in expression position and
`paste::item!` for macros in item position.

Within either one, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to form a
single identifier.

```
// Macro in item position: at module scope or inside of an impl block.
item!
```
## More elaborate examples

This program demonstrates how you may want to bundle a paste invocation inside
of a more convenient user-facing macro of your own. Here the `routes!(A, B)`
macro expands to a vector containing `ROUTE_A` and `ROUTE_B`.

```
const ROUTE_A: &str = "/a";
const ROUTE_B: &str = "/b";
```
The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields.

```
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!;
```
## Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an interpolated
segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

There are two entry points, `paste::expr!` for macros in expression position and
`paste::item!` for macros in item position.

Within either one, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to form a
single identifier.

```
// Macro in item position: at module scope or inside of an impl block.
item!
```
## More elaborate examples

This program demonstrates how you may want to bundle a paste invocation inside
of a more convenient user-facing macro of your own. Here the `routes!(A, B)`
macro expands to a vector containing `ROUTE_A` and `ROUTE_B`.

```
const ROUTE_A: &str = "/a";
const ROUTE_B: &str = "/b";
```
The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields.

```
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!;
```
## Case conversion

Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an interpolated
segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For example, `[<ld_ $reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked with $reg=`Bc`.

Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING_CASE.

The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`

---

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```

```
This approach works with any stable or nightly Rust compiler 1.30+.

# paste 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste/0.1.0

# Macros for all your token pasting needs

The nightly-only [ concat_idents!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.concat_idents.html) macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.

This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro, including using pasted identifiers to define new items.

```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
This approach works with any stable or nightly Rust compiler 1.30+.

## Pasting identifiers

There are two entry points, `paste::expr!` for macros in expression position and
`paste::item!` for macros in item position.

Within either one, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to form a
single identifier.

```
extern crate paste;
// Macro in item position: at module scope or inside of an impl block.
item!
```
## More elaborate examples

This program demonstrates how you may want to bundle a paste invocation inside
of a more convenient user-facing macro of your own. Here the `routes!(A, B)`
macro expands to a vector containing `ROUTE_A` and `ROUTE_B`.

```
extern crate paste;
const ROUTE_A: &str = "/a";
const ROUTE_B: &str = "/b";
```
The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields.

```
extern crate paste;
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!;
```
## Limitations

- As a consequence of hygiene, a concatenated identifier may not be used to
refer to a captured local variable ([#1](https://github.com/dtolnay/paste/issues/1)).

# paste 1.0.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste/latest/source/README.md

```
Macros for all your token pasting needs
=======================================
[<img alt="github" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/github-dtolnay/paste-8da0cb?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=555555&logo=github" height="20">](https://github.com/dtolnay/paste)
[<img alt="crates.io" src="https://img.shields.io/crates/v/paste.svg?style=for-the-badge&color=fc8d62&logo=rust" height="20">](https://crates.io/crates/paste)
[<img alt="docs.rs" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/docs.rs-paste-66c2a5?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=555555&logo=docs.rs" height="20">](https://docs.rs/paste)
[<img alt="build status" src="https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/dtolnay/paste/ci.yml?branch=master&style=for-the-badge" height="20">](https://github.com/dtolnay/paste/actions?query=branch%3Amaster)
The nightly-only [`concat_idents!`] macro in the Rust standard library is
notoriously underpowered in that its concatenated identifiers can only refer to
existing items, they can never be used to define something new.
This crate provides a flexible way to paste together identifiers in a macro,
including using pasted identifiers to define new items.
```toml
[dependencies]
paste = "1.0"
```
This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.31+.
Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`...`>]` are pasted together to
form a single identifier.
```rust
use paste::paste;
paste! {
}
fn main() {
}
```
The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct
fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste
invocation inside of a macro\_rules macro.
```rust
use paste::paste;
macro_rules! make_a_struct_and_getters {
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!(S { a, b, c });
fn call_some_getters(s: &S) -> bool {
}
```
Use `$var:lower` or `$var:upper` in the segment list to convert an interpolated
segment to lower- or uppercase as part of the paste. For example, `[<ld_
$reg:lower _expr>]` would paste to `ld_bc_expr` if invoked with $reg=`Bc`.
Use `$var:snake` to convert CamelCase input to snake\_case.
Use `$var:camel` to convert snake\_case to CamelCase.
These compose, so for example `$var:snake:upper` would give you SCREAMING\_CASE.
The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [`str::to_lowercase`] and
[`str::to_uppercase`].
Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #\[doc ...\] attribute are implicitly
concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.
```rust
use paste::paste;
macro_rules! method_new {
}
pub struct Paste {}
method_new!(Paste);  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
```
```

---

# paste-test-suite 0.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/paste-test-suite/0.0.0/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# rustversion 1.0.22 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rustversion/1.0.22

# Compiler version cfg

This crate provides macros for conditional compilation according to rustc
compiler version, analogous to [ #[cfg(...)]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg-attribute) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg_attr-attribute)

`#[cfg_attr(...)]````
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Selectors

-
`#[rustversion::stable]`— True on any stable compiler.
-
`#[rustversion::stable(1.34)]`— True on exactly the specified stable compiler.
-
`#[rustversion::beta]`— True on any beta compiler.
-
`#[rustversion::nightly]`— True on any nightly compiler or dev build.
-
`#[rustversion::nightly(2025-01-01)]`— True on exactly one nightly.
-
`#[rustversion::since(1.34)]`— True on that stable release and any later compiler, including beta and nightly.
-
`#[rustversion::since(2025-01-01)]`— True on that nightly and all newer ones.
-
`#[rustversion::before(`version or date`)]`— Negative of*#[rustversion::since(...)]*.
-
`#[rustversion::not(`selector`)]`— Negative of any selector; for example*#[rustversion::not(nightly)]*.
-
`#[rustversion::any(`selectors...`)]`— True if any of the comma-separated selectors is true; for example*#[rustversion::any(stable, beta)]*.
-
`#[rustversion::all(`selectors...`)]`— True if all of the comma-separated selectors are true; for example*#[rustversion::all(since(1.31), before(1.34))]*.
-
`#[rustversion::attr(`selector`,`attribute`)]`— For conditional inclusion of attributes; analogous to`cfg_attr`.
-
`rustversion::cfg!(`selector`)`— An expression form of any of the above attributes; for example*if rustversion::cfg!(any(stable, beta)) { ... }*.

## Use cases

Providing additional trait impls as types are stabilized in the standard library
without breaking compatibility with older compilers; in this case Pin<P>
stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2019/02/28/Rust-1.33.0.html#pinning):

```
use Pin;
```
Similar but for language features; the ability to control alignment greater than
1 of packed structs was stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/RELEASES.md#version-1330-2019-02-28).

```
;
```
Augmenting code with `const` as const impls are stabilized in the standard
library. This use of `const` as an attribute is recognized as a special case by
the rustversion::attr macro.

```
use Duration;
```
Emitting Cargo cfg directives from a build script. Note that this requires
listing `rustversion` under `[build-dependencies]` in Cargo.toml, not
`[dependencies]`.

```
// build.rs
```
```
// src/lib.rs
extern crate alloc;
```

# rustversion 1.0.22 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rustversion/1.0.22/source/

#
                    rustversion 1.0.22

                Conditional compilation according to rustc compiler version

---

# rustversion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rustversion/1.0.22/target-redirect/rustversion/

## Expand description

This crate provides macros for conditional compilation according to rustc
compiler version, analogous to [ #[cfg(...)]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg-attribute) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg_attr-attribute)

`#[cfg_attr(...)]`[§](https://docs.rs#selectors)Selectors

- `#[rustversion::stable]`
 True on any stable compiler.
- `#[rustversion::stable(1.34)]`
 True on exactly the specified stable compiler.
- `#[rustversion::beta]`
 True on any beta compiler.
- `#[rustversion::nightly]`
 True on any nightly compiler or dev build.
- `#[rustversion::nightly(2025-01-01)]`
 True on exactly one nightly.
- `#[rustversion::since(1.34)]`
 True on that stable release and any later compiler, including beta and nightly.
- `#[rustversion::since(2025-01-01)]`
 True on that nightly and all newer ones.
- `#[rustversion::before(`- *version or date*- `)]`
 Negative of- *#[rustversion::since(...)]*.
- `#[rustversion::not(`- *selector*- `)]`
 Negative of any selector; for example- *#[rustversion::not(nightly)]*.
- `#[rustversion::any(`- *selectors...*- `)]`
 True if any of the comma-separated selectors is true; for example- *#[rustversion::any(stable, beta)]*.
- `#[rustversion::all(`- *selectors...*- `)]`
 True if all of the comma-separated selectors are true; for example- *#[rustversion::all(since(1.31), before(1.34))]*.
- `#[rustversion::attr(`- *selector*- `,`- *attribute*- `)]`
 For conditional inclusion of attributes; analogous to- `cfg_attr`.
- `rustversion::cfg!(`- *selector*- `)`
 An expression form of any of the above attributes; for example- *if rustversion::cfg!(any(stable, beta)) { ... }*.

[§](https://docs.rs#use-cases)Use cases

Providing additional trait impls as types are stabilized in the standard library
without breaking compatibility with older compilers; in this case Pin<P>
stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2019/02/28/Rust-1.33.0.html#pinning):

```
#[rustversion::since(1.33)]
use std::pin::Pin;
#[rustversion::since(1.33)]
impl<P: MyTrait> MyTrait for Pin<P> {
    /* ... */
}
```
Similar but for language features; the ability to control alignment greater than
1 of packed structs was stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/RELEASES.md#version-1330-2019-02-28).

```
#[rustversion::attr(before(1.33), repr(packed))]
#[rustversion::attr(since(1.33), repr(packed(2)))]
struct Six(i16, i32);
fn main() {
    println!("{}", std::mem::align_of::<Six>());
}
```
Augmenting code with `const` as const impls are stabilized in the standard
library. This use of `const` as an attribute is recognized as a special case
by the rustversion::attr macro.

```
use std::time::Duration;
#[rustversion::attr(since(1.32), const)]
fn duration_as_days(dur: Duration) -> u64 {
    dur.as_secs() / 60 / 60 / 24
}
```
Emitting Cargo cfg directives from a build script. Note that this requires
listing `rustversion` under `[build-dependencies]` in Cargo.toml, not
`[dependencies]`.

```
// build.rs
fn main() {
    if rustversion::cfg!(since(1.36)) {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=no_std");
    }
}
```
```
// src/lib.rs
#![cfg_attr(no_std, no_std)]
#[cfg(no_std)]
extern crate alloc;
```

---
