# relentless/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Retry and polling for Rust — with composable strategies, policy reuse, and
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! first-class support for polling workflows where `Ok(_)` doesn't always mean
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! "done."
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! Most retry libraries handle the simple case well: call a function, retry on
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! error, back off. `relentless` handles that too, but it also handles the cases
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! those libraries make awkward:
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! - **Polling**, where `Ok("pending")` means "keep going" and you need
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!   [`.until(predicate)`](SyncRetryBuilder::until) rather than just retrying errors.
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! - **Policy reuse**, where a single [`RetryPolicy`] captures your retry rules and
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!   gets shared across multiple call sites — no duplicated builder chains.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! - **Strategy composition**, where
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!   `wait::fixed(50ms) + wait::exponential(100ms)` and
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!   `stop::attempts(5) | stop::elapsed(2s)` express complex behavior in one line.
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! - **Hooks and stats**, where you observe the retry lifecycle (logging, metrics)
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!   without restructuring your retry logic.
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! All of this works in sync and async code, across `std`, `no_std`, and `wasm`
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! targets.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! # Quick start
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! The [`RetryExt`] extension trait is the fastest way to add retries. Defaults:
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! 3 attempts, exponential backoff from 100 ms, retry on any `Err`.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ```
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! use relentless::RetryExt;
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! let result = (|| Ok::<_, &str>(42)).retry().sleep(|_| {}).call();
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), 42);
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! ```
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! The [`retry`] and [`retry_async`] free functions are equivalent, with the
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! added ability to capture retry loop state via the [`RetryState`] argument:
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! ```
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! use relentless::retry;
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! let result = retry(|state| {
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!     if state.attempt >= 2 { Ok(state.attempt) } else { Err("not yet") }
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! })
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! .sleep(|_| {})
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! .call();
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), 2);
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! ```
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! # Customizing retry behavior
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! Builder methods control **when** to retry, **how long** to wait, and **when**
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! to stop:
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! ```
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! use core::time::Duration;
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! use relentless::{Wait, retry, predicate, stop, wait};
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! let result = retry(|_| Err::<(), &str>("boom"))
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!     .when(predicate::error(|e: &&str| *e == "boom"))
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!     .wait(
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!         wait::exponential(Duration::from_millis(100))
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!             .full_jitter()
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!             .cap(Duration::from_secs(5)),
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!     )
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!     .stop(stop::attempts(3))
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!     .sleep(|_| {})
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!     .call();
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! assert!(result.is_err());
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! ```
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! To bound the **total** wall-clock time across all attempts and sleeps, add
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! [`.timeout(dur)`](SyncRetryBuilder::timeout). It OR-folds an elapsed deadline
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! into the stop strategy and clamps each inter-attempt sleep to the remaining
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! budget; it does not interrupt an attempt already running. See [Cancellation]
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! for the runtime-agnostic deadline pattern.
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! [Cancellation]: #cancellation
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! # Policy reuse
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! [`RetryPolicy`] captures retry rules once. Compose wait strategies with `+`
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! and stop strategies with `|` or `&`.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! ```
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! use core::time::Duration;
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! use relentless::{RetryPolicy, stop, wait};
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//!
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! let policy = RetryPolicy::new()
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!     .wait(
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!         wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(50))
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!             + wait::exponential(Duration::from_millis(100)),
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!     )
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!     .stop(stop::attempts(5) | stop::elapsed(Duration::from_secs(30)));
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! // Same policy, different operations.
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! let a = policy.retry(|_| Ok::<_, &str>("a")).sleep(|_| {}).call();
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! let b = policy.retry(|_| Ok::<_, &str>("b")).sleep(|_| {}).call();
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! assert_eq!(a.unwrap(), "a");
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! assert_eq!(b.unwrap(), "b");
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! ```
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//!
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! # Polling for a condition
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//!
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! Use [`.until(predicate)`](SyncRetryBuilder::until) to keep retrying until a
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! success condition is met. Unlike [`.when()`](SyncRetryBuilder::when), which
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! retries on matching outcomes, `.until()` retries on everything *except* the
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! matching outcome.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//!
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! ```
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! use relentless::{RetryPolicy, predicate};
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! enum Status { Pending, Done }
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! let mut count = 0;
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//! let result = RetryPolicy::new()
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//!     .until(predicate::ok(|s: &Status| *s == Status::Done))
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!     .retry(|_| {
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!         count += 1;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!         Ok::<_, &str>(if count >= 2 { Status::Done } else { Status::Pending })
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!     })
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!     .sleep(|_| {})
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//!     .call();
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//! assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), Status::Done);
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//! ```
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! # Hooks and stats
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! ```
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//! use relentless::retry;
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! let (result, stats) = retry(|_| Ok::<_, &str>("done"))
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!     .before_attempt(|state| {
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!         if state.attempt > 1 {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!             println!("retrying (attempt {})", state.attempt);
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!         }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!     })
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!     .after_attempt(|state| {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!         if let Err(e) = state.outcome {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!             eprintln!("attempt {} failed: {e}", state.attempt);
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!         }
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!     })
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!     .sleep(|_| {})
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!     .with_stats()
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//!     .call();
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! println!("attempts: {}, total wait: {:?}", stats.attempts, stats.total_wait);
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//! ```
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//!
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! # Error handling
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//!
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! The retry loop returns `Ok(T)` on success. On failure it returns
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! [`RetryError`], which distinguishes between exhaustion (stop strategy fired)
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! and rejection (predicate deemed the error non-retryable):
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//!
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//! ```
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! use relentless::{retry, RetryError};
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//! match retry(|_| Err::<(), &str>("boom")).sleep(|_| {}).call() {
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!     Ok(val) => println!("success: {val:?}"),
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!     Err(RetryError::Exhausted { last }) => {
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!         println!("gave up: {last:?}");
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!     }
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!     Err(RetryError::Rejected { last }) => {
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//!         println!("non-retryable: {last}");
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!     }
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//!     // `RetryError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`; match future variants here.
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!     Err(_) => {}
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//! }
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! ```
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! # Cancellation
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! By design, the retry engine has no built-in cancellation primitive — it
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! composes with the cancellation your environment already provides, observed at
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! attempt boundaries (a running operation or sleep is never interrupted
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! mid-flight).
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//!
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//! - **Async:** the future returned by [`.call()`](AsyncRetryExec::call) is
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//!   cancel-safe — drop it (e.g. via `tokio::time::timeout` or `select!`) to
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!   stop at the next `.await`. Note `on_exit` does **not** fire on drop; use
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//!   `Drop` on your own types for guaranteed cleanup. See the `async-cancel`
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//!   example.
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! - **Sync:** bound the wall-clock with [`.timeout()`](SyncRetryBuilder::timeout),
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//!   or check a flag inside the operation and return a sentinel error. With the
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!   default `any_error()` predicate that sentinel is *retried*, so make it
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//!   non-retryable via [`.when()`](SyncRetryBuilder::when) (it then terminates as
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//!   [`RetryError::Rejected`]). See the `sync-cancel` example.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//!
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! # Custom wait strategies
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//!
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! Implement [`Wait`] to build your own wait strategies. All combinators
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! ([`.cap()`](Wait::cap), [`.full_jitter()`](Wait::full_jitter),
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! [`.chain()`](Wait::chain), `+`) work on any `Wait` implementor.
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//!
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//! ```
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//! use core::time::Duration;
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! use relentless::{RetryState, Wait, wait};
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! struct CustomWait(Duration);
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//!
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//! impl Wait for CustomWait {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//!     fn next_wait(&self, _state: &RetryState) -> Duration {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!         self.0
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//!     }
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//! }
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! let strategy = CustomWait(Duration::from_millis(20))
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//!     .cap(Duration::from_millis(15))
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//!     .chain(wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(50)), 2);
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! let state = RetryState::new(3, None);
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//! assert_eq!(strategy.next_wait(&state), Duration::from_millis(50));
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! ```
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//! # Feature flags
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//!
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//! | Flag | Purpose |
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//! |------|---------|
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! | `std` (default) | `std::thread::sleep` fallback, `Instant` elapsed clock, `std::error::Error` on `RetryError` |
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//! | `alloc` | Boxed policies, closure elapsed clocks, multiple hooks per point |
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! | `tokio-sleep` | `sleep::tokio()` async sleep adapter |
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//! | `embassy-sleep` | `sleep::embassy()` async sleep adapter |
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//! | `gloo-timers-sleep` | `sleep::gloo()` async sleep adapter (wasm32) |
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//! | `futures-timer-sleep` | `sleep::futures_timer()` async sleep adapter |
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//! Async retry does not require `alloc`. Sync `std` builds automatically fall
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! back to `std::thread::sleep`, so `.sleep(...)` is optional.
[232](https://docs.rs#232)
[233](https://docs.rs#233)#![no_std]
[234](https://docs.rs#234)#![forbid(unsafe_code)]

[283](https://docs.rs#283)/// Commonly used traits, glob-imported to enable the builder DSL.
[284](https://docs.rs#284)///
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// The combinator methods (`.cap()`, `.full_jitter()`, `.chain()` on [`Wait`];
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// `.or()`/`.and()` on [`Stop`] and [`Predicate`]) and the closure extensions
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// (`.retry()` on [`RetryExt`], `.retry_async()` on [`AsyncRetryExt`]) are trait
[288](https://docs.rs#288)/// methods, so the trait must be in scope to call them. Glob-import this module
[289](https://docs.rs#289)/// to bring them all in at once:
[290](https://docs.rs#290)///
[291](https://docs.rs#291)/// ```
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// use relentless::prelude::*;
[293](https://docs.rs#293)/// use relentless::wait;
[294](https://docs.rs#294)/// use core::time::Duration;
[295](https://docs.rs#295)///
[296](https://docs.rs#296)/// // `.full_jitter()` and `.cap()` resolve without naming `Wait`.
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// let _ = wait::exponential(Duration::from_millis(100))
[298](https://docs.rs#298)///     .full_jitter()
[299](https://docs.rs#299)///     .cap(Duration::from_secs(5));
[300](https://docs.rs#300)/// ```
[301](https://docs.rs#301)///

[303](https://docs.rs#303)/// re-exported here; import them explicitly by name.

[306](https://docs.rs#306)}

[308](https://docs.rs#308)/// Returns a [`SyncRetryBuilder`] with default policy: `attempts(3)`,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// `exponential(100ms)`, `any_error()`.
[310](https://docs.rs#310)///

[334](https://docs.rs#334)    E,
[335](https://docs.rs#335)>
[336](https://docs.rs#336)where
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    F: FnMut(RetryState) -> Result<T, E>,
[338](https://docs.rs#338){

[340](https://docs.rs#340)}
[341](https://docs.rs#341)
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// Returns an [`AsyncRetryBuilder`] with default policy: `attempts(3)`,

[344](https://docs.rs#344)///

[353](https://docs.rs#353)/// let result = retry_async(|_| async { Ok::<u32, &str>(42) })
[354](https://docs.rs#354)///     .sleep(|_dur: Duration| async {})

[373](https://docs.rs#373)    E,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)>

[378](https://docs.rs#378){

# SyncRetryExec in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/struct.SyncRetryExec.html

`pub struct SyncRetryExec<Policy, BA, AA, OX, F, SleepFn, T, E> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Sync retry execution object, generic over how the policy is stored.

A single engine drives both entry points:

- `SyncRetry`- `Policy = &RetryPolicy<S, W, P>`), created by- `RetryPolicy::retry`
- `SyncRetryBuilder`- `Policy = RetryPolicy<S, W, P>`), created by- `crate::RetryExt::retry`

Methods that only make sense when the policy is owned (`stop`, `wait`,
`when`, `until`) are implemented separately on the owned alias.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/execution/sync_exec.rs.html#209-212)#### pub fn [elapsed_clock_fn](https://docs.rs#method.elapsed_clock_fn)(self, clock: impl [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)() -> [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html) + 'static) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/execution/sync_exec.rs.html#209-212)

#### pub fn [elapsed_clock_fn](https://docs.rs#method.elapsed_clock_fn)(self, clock: impl [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)() -> [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html) + 'static) -> Self

Configures a custom elapsed clock from a boxed closure.

This variant supports closures with captures for test clocks and
runtime state. Requires the `alloc` feature.

Sets a wall-clock budget for the entire retry execution.

This is a **boundary check, not a preemptive timeout.** It is evaluated
between attempts: the next inter-attempt sleep is clamped so the loop
terminates close to the deadline, and the loop stops once the elapsed
time exceeds `dur`. It **cannot** interrupt an operation or a sleep that
is already in progress.

For a hard wall-clock cancellation that can preempt in-flight work, wrap
the retry future in your async runtime’s timeout (e.g.
`tokio::time::timeout`); see the `async-cancel` example.

# RetryPolicy in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/struct.RetryPolicy.html

`pub struct RetryPolicy<S = `[StopAfterAttempts](https://docs.rs/stop/struct.StopAfterAttempts.html), W = [WaitExponential](https://docs.rs/wait/struct.WaitExponential.html), P = [PredicateAnyError](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateAnyError.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

Reusable retry configuration.

`RetryPolicy` stores retry strategies and can be reused across multiple
operations. Hook callbacks are configured per-execution on `SyncRetry` and
`AsyncRetry` builders.

Construction options:

- `RetryPolicy::new`- `attempts(3)`,- `exponential(100ms)`,- `any_error()`.
- `Default::default`- `new()`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::{RetryPolicy, stop, wait};
use core::time::Duration;
let policy = RetryPolicy::new()
    .stop(stop::attempts(3))
    .wait(wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(5)));
let _ = policy.retry(|_| Err::<(), _>("fail")).sleep(|_dur| {}).call();
```

    .retry_async(|_| async { Ok::<u32, &str>(1) })
    .sleep(|_dur: Duration| async {});
let _ = retry;
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/mod.rs.html#138-147)#### pub fn [until](https://docs.rs#method.until)<NewPredicate>(
    self,
    predicate: NewPredicate,
) -> [RetryPolicy](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html)<S, W, [PredicateUntil](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateUntil.html)<NewPredicate>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/mod.rs.html#138-147)

#### pub fn [until](https://docs.rs#method.until)<NewPredicate>(
    self,
    predicate: NewPredicate,
) -> [RetryPolicy](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html)<S, W, [PredicateUntil](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateUntil.html)<NewPredicate>>

Sets a predicate that retries *until* `p.should_retry()` returns `true`.

Wraps `p` in [ predicate::PredicateUntil](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateUntil.html),
negating its result. Natural for polling:

`.until(ok(|s| s.is_ready()))` reads “retry until ready.”[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/mod.rs.html#192-204)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/mod.rs.html#192-204)

Erases the generic stop and wait parameters behind trait objects, leaving the predicate type intact.

This produces a single, nameable type —
`RetryPolicy<Box<dyn Stop + Send>, Box<dyn Wait + Send>, P>` — suitable
for a struct field or a heterogeneous collection, without spelling out
the full nested stop/wait generics.

The predicate is deliberately **not** erased. The default predicate
([ PredicateAnyError](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateAnyError.html)) implements

[for](https://docs.rs/predicate/trait.Predicate.html)

`Predicate<T, E>`*every*

`T` and `E`, so a default-predicate boxed
policy can be reused across operations with **different**success and error types. Boxing the predicate (as

`Box<dyn Predicate<T, E>>`) would
pin it to one `(T, E)` and defeat that reuse — which is why only stop and
wait are erased here.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

Store one customized policy in a struct and reuse it across operations
whose `Ok` types differ:

```
use core::time::Duration;
use relentless::{RetryPolicy, Stop, Wait, stop, wait};
struct Client {
    policy: RetryPolicy<Box<dyn Stop + Send>, Box<dyn Wait + Send>>,
}
let client = Client {
    policy: RetryPolicy::new()
        .stop(stop::attempts(3) | stop::elapsed(Duration::from_secs(2)))
        .wait(wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(10)))
        .boxed(),
};
let a: Result<u32, _> = client.policy.retry(|_| Ok::<u32, &str>(1)).sleep(|_| {}).call();
let b: Result<(), _> = client.policy.retry(|_| Ok::<(), &str>(())).sleep(|_| {}).call();
assert_eq!(a.unwrap(), 1);
assert_eq!(b.unwrap(), ());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/mod.rs.html#222-232)#### pub fn [boxed_local](https://docs.rs#method.boxed_local)(
    self,
) -> [RetryPolicy](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Stop](https://docs.rs/stop/trait.Stop.html) + 'static>, [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Wait](https://docs.rs/wait/trait.Wait.html) + 'static>, P>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/mod.rs.html#222-232)

#### pub fn [boxed_local](https://docs.rs#method.boxed_local)(
    self,
) -> [RetryPolicy](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Stop](https://docs.rs/stop/trait.Stop.html) + 'static>, [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Wait](https://docs.rs/wait/trait.Wait.html) + 'static>, P>

Erases the generic stop and wait parameters behind local trait objects, leaving the predicate type intact.

Like [ boxed](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html#method.boxed) but without

`Send` bounds, for policies that
do not cross thread boundaries.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use relentless::RetryPolicy;
let policy = RetryPolicy::new().boxed_local();
let _ = policy.retry(|_| Err::<(), _>("fail")).sleep(|_| {}).call();
```

# RetryExt in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/trait.RetryExt.html

`pub trait RetryExt<T, E>: `[FnMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnMut.html)() -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, E> + [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {

}## Expand description

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/ext/sync_builder.rs.html#32)#### fn [retry](https://docs.rs#tymethod.retry)(self) -> [DefaultSyncRetryBuilder](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultSyncRetryBuilder.html)<Self, T, E>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/ext/sync_builder.rs.html#32)

#### fn [retry](https://docs.rs#tymethod.retry)(self) -> [DefaultSyncRetryBuilder](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultSyncRetryBuilder.html)<Self, T, E>

Starts an owned sync retry builder from [ RetryPolicy::default()](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html#method.default).

This means extension-based retries default to:

- `stop::attempts(3)`
- exponential backoff starting at 100ms
- retry on any error

In `std` builds, `.call()` works without `.sleep(...)`. The example
below still configures `.sleep(...)` so it also works in non-`std`
documentation tests.

```
use relentless::RetryExt;
let _ = (|| Ok::<(), &str>(()))
    .retry()
    .sleep(|_| {})
    .call();
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# retry in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/fn.retry.html

```
pub fn retry<F, T, E>(
    op: F,
) ->
```
[SyncRetryBuilder](https://docs.rs/type.SyncRetryBuilder.html)<[StopAfterAttempts](https://docs.rs/stop/struct.StopAfterAttempts.html), [WaitExponential](https://docs.rs/wait/struct.WaitExponential.html), [PredicateAnyError](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateAnyError.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), F, NoSyncSleep, T, E>## Expand description

Returns a [ SyncRetryBuilder](https://docs.rs/type.SyncRetryBuilder.html) with default policy:

`attempts(3)`,
`exponential(100ms)`, `any_error()`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::{retry, stop};
let result = retry(|_| Ok::<u32, &str>(42))
    .stop(stop::attempts(1))
    .sleep(|_| {})
    .call();
assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), 42);
```

# retry_async in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/fn.retry_async.html

```
pub fn retry_async<F, T, E, Fut>(
    op: F,
) ->
```
[AsyncRetryBuilder](https://docs.rs/type.AsyncRetryBuilder.html)<[StopAfterAttempts](https://docs.rs/stop/struct.StopAfterAttempts.html), [WaitExponential](https://docs.rs/wait/struct.WaitExponential.html), [PredicateAnyError](https://docs.rs/predicate/struct.PredicateAnyError.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), F, Fut, NoAsyncSleep, T, E>## Expand description

Returns an [ AsyncRetryBuilder](https://docs.rs/type.AsyncRetryBuilder.html) with default policy:

`attempts(3)`,
`exponential(100ms)`, `any_error()`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use core::time::Duration;
use relentless::retry_async;
// Async terminates with `.call().await` (mirroring the sync `.call()`).
let result = retry_async(|_| async { Ok::<u32, &str>(42) })
    .sleep(|_dur: Duration| async {})
    .call()
    .await;
assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), 42);
```

# RetryState in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/struct.RetryState.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct RetryState {
    pub attempt:
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub elapsed: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>,
    pub previous_delay: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>,
}## Expand description

Non-generic retry context passed to [ Stop::should_stop](https://docs.rs/stop/trait.Stop.html#tymethod.should_stop),

[, the operation, and the](https://docs.rs/wait/trait.Wait.html#tymethod.next_wait)

`Wait::next_wait``before_attempt` hook.This contains only the timing and counting fields that stop/wait strategies
need. It deliberately excludes the operation’s outcome, keeping `Stop` and
`Wait` decoupled from the operation’s `Result<T, E>` type.

The operation receives `RetryState` by value (it is `Copy`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::RetryState;
use core::time::Duration;
fn log_state(state: &RetryState) {
    println!("attempt {} elapsed {:?}", state.attempt, state.elapsed);
}
```
## Fields (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

## This struct is marked as non-exhaustive

`Struct { .. }` syntax; cannot be matched against without a wildcard `..`; and struct update syntax will not work.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.attempt)

`attempt: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The 1-indexed attempt number.

For the operation and `before_attempt`, this is the attempt about to start.
For `Stop` and `Wait`, this is the just-completed attempt.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.elapsed)

`elapsed: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>Wall-clock time elapsed since the first attempt began.
`None` when no clock is available (e.g. `no_std` without a time source).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.previous_delay)

`previous_delay: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>The delay applied before this attempt — the previous inter-attempt sleep,
after cap/timeout clamping — or `None` on the first attempt.

Wait strategies use this for feedback backoff. For example, decorrelated
jitter computes `random(base, previous_delay * 3)`.

# RetryError in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/enum.RetryError.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum RetryError<T, E> {
    Exhausted {
        last:
```
[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, E>,
    },
    Rejected {
        last: E,
    },
}## Expand description

Error returned when a retry loop terminates without producing an accepted result.

`RetryError` implements [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) and (with

`std`)
[, so the simplest handling is to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/error/trait.Error.html)

`std::error::Error`**propagate it directly**—

`?` into `anyhow::Error`/`Box<dyn Error>`, or a `thiserror`
`#[from]` field — rather than unwrapping it.Note that [ Exhausted::last](https://docs.rs/enum.RetryError.html#variant.Exhausted) is the full

`Result<T, E>` (a polling loop can exhaust on a non-accepted `Ok`), **not**the bare error. Printing the

`RetryError` itself uses `Display`; destructure
`last` only when you specifically need the final outcome. To collapse to the
underlying error use [.](https://docs.rs/enum.RetryError.html#method.into_last_error)

`into_last_error`[§](https://docs.rs#type-parameters)Type Parameters

- `T`: The- `Ok`value type from the retried operation.
- `E`: The error type from the retried operation.

Variant selection follows the retry predicate and terminal outcome:

- `RetryError::Exhausted`
- `RetryError::Rejected`- `Err`outcome as terminal (did not request retry).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::RetryError;
let err: RetryError<(), String> = RetryError::Exhausted {
    last: Err("connection refused".to_string()),
};
println!("{}", err);
```
## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Exhausted)

### Exhausted

Retries exhausted — the stop strategy fired while the predicate still wanted to retry. The last outcome is preserved.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Rejected)

### Rejected

The predicate accepted an `Err` outcome as terminal (did not
request retry).

# AsyncRetryExec in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/struct.AsyncRetryExec.html

`pub struct AsyncRetryExec<Policy, BA, AA, OX, F, Fut, SleepImpl, T, E, SleepFut = `[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

Async retry execution object, generic over how the policy is stored.

A single engine drives both entry points:

- `AsyncRetry`- `Policy = &RetryPolicy<S, W, P>`), created by- `RetryPolicy::retry_async`
- `AsyncRetryBuilder`- `Policy = RetryPolicy<S, W, P>`), created by- `crate::AsyncRetryExt::retry_async`

Methods that only make sense when the policy is owned (`stop`, `wait`,
`when`, `until`) are implemented separately on the owned alias.

This future is single-use. Polling after completion is misuse and always panics.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

#### pub fn [call](https://docs.rs#method.call)(self) -> impl [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [RetryError](https://docs.rs/enum.RetryError.html)<T, E>>>

Runs the configured retry loop, returning a future that resolves to the final result.

This is the async terminator, mirroring the synchronous
[ SyncRetry::call](https://docs.rs/struct.SyncRetryExec.html#method.call). Dropping the returned future
cancels the loop at the next

`.await` point (cancel-safe); `on_exit` does
not fire on drop.[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/policy/ext/async_builder.rs.html#183-248)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AsyncRetryExec%3CRetryPolicy%3CS,+W,+P%3E,+BA,+AA,+OX,+F,+Fut,+SleepImpl,+T,+E,+SleepFut%3E)### impl<S, W, P, BA, AA, OX, F, Fut, SleepImpl, T, E, SleepFut> [AsyncRetryExec](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncRetryExec.html)<[RetryPolicy](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryPolicy.html)<S, W, P>, BA, AA, OX, F, Fut, SleepImpl, T, E, SleepFut>

}## Expand description

Computes the delay duration between retry attempts.

Implementations receive the current [ RetryState](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryState.html) (attempt count and
elapsed time) and return the duration to sleep before the next attempt.
Wait strategies never inspect the operation’s outcome — they depend
only on timing and counting, so the same strategy can be reused across
any operation type.

Composition and builder methods are provided directly on the trait with
`where Self: Sized` bounds.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::{RetryState, Wait};
use core::time::Duration;
struct FixedDelay(Duration);
impl Wait for FixedDelay {
    fn next_wait(&self, _state: &RetryState) -> Duration {
        self.0
    }
}
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Uses this strategy for the first `after` attempts, then switches to `other`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/wait/mod.rs.html#84-89)#### fn [add](https://docs.rs#method.add)<W2: [Wait](https://docs.rs/trait.Wait.html)>(self, other: W2) -> [WaitCombine](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitCombine.html)<Self, W2>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/wait/mod.rs.html#84-89)

#### fn [add](https://docs.rs#method.add)<W2: [Wait](https://docs.rs/trait.Wait.html)>(self, other: W2) -> [WaitCombine](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitCombine.html)<Self, W2>

Adds another wait strategy to this one.

This is the named equivalent of the `+` operator — returns
the sum of both strategies’ outputs (saturating on overflow).

```
use relentless::{Wait, wait};
use core::time::Duration;
// These are equivalent:
let a = wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(50)).add(wait::exponential(Duration::from_millis(100)));
let b = wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(50)) + wait::exponential(Duration::from_millis(100));
```
Adds uniformly distributed jitter in `[0, max_jitter]`.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

}## Expand description

Examines the outcome of an operation and decides whether to retry.

Composition methods are provided directly on the trait with
`where Self: Sized` bounds.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::Predicate;
struct RetryOnError;
impl Predicate<String, &str> for RetryOnError {
    fn should_retry(&self, outcome: &Result<String, &str>) -> bool {
        outcome.is_err()
    }
}
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/predicate/mod.rs.html#50-55)#### fn [or](https://docs.rs#method.or)<P: [Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html)<T, E>>(self, other: P) -> [PredicateAny](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAny.html)<Self, P>

#### fn [or](https://docs.rs#method.or)<P: [Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html)<T, E>>(self, other: P) -> [PredicateAny](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAny.html)<Self, P>

Returns a predicate that retries when either side retries.

This is the named equivalent of the `|` operator.

```
use relentless::{Predicate, predicate};
// These are equivalent:
let a = predicate::error(|e: &&str| *e == "retry").or(predicate::ok(|v: &u32| *v < 2));
let b = predicate::error(|e: &&str| *e == "retry") | predicate::ok(|v: &u32| *v < 2);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/predicate/mod.rs.html#69-74)#### fn [and](https://docs.rs#method.and)<P: [Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html)<T, E>>(self, other: P) -> [PredicateAll](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAll.html)<Self, P>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/relentless/predicate/mod.rs.html#69-74)

#### fn [and](https://docs.rs#method.and)<P: [Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html)<T, E>>(self, other: P) -> [PredicateAll](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAll.html)<Self, P>

Returns a predicate that retries only when both sides retry.

This is the named equivalent of the `&` operator.

```
use relentless::{Predicate, predicate};
// These are equivalent:
let a = predicate::error(|e: &&str| *e == "retry").and(predicate::ok(|v: &u32| *v < 2));
let b = predicate::error(|e: &&str| *e == "retry") & predicate::ok(|v: &u32| *v < 2);
```

# Sleeper in relentless::sleep - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/sleep/trait.Sleeper.html

```
pub trait Sleeper {
    type
```
[Sleep](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Sleep): [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>;
    // Required method
    fn [sleep](https://docs.rs#tymethod.sleep)(&self, dur: [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)) -> Self::[Sleep](https://docs.rs/trait.Sleeper.html#associatedtype.Sleep);
}## Expand description

Async sleep abstraction used by the retry engine between attempts.

Only the async execution engine uses this trait; the sync engine calls a blocking sleep function directly.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::Sleeper;
use core::time::Duration;
use core::future::Future;
use core::pin::Pin;
use core::task::{Context, Poll};
struct NoOpSleep;
impl Future for NoOpSleep {
    type Output = ();
    fn poll(self: Pin<&mut Self>, _cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<()> {
        Poll::Ready(())
    }
}
struct NoOpSleeper;
impl Sleeper for NoOpSleeper {
    type Sleep = NoOpSleep;
    fn sleep(&self, _dur: Duration) -> Self::Sleep {
        NoOpSleep
    }
}
```
## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Stop in relentless::stop - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/stop/trait.Stop.html

```
pub trait Stop {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[should_stop](https://docs.rs#tymethod.should_stop)(&self, state: &[RetryState](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryState.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html);
    // Provided methods
    fn [or](https://docs.rs#method.or)<S: [Stop](https://docs.rs/trait.Stop.html)>(self, other: S) -> [StopAny](https://docs.rs/struct.StopAny.html)<Self, S>
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) { ... }
[and](https://docs.rs#method.and)<S: [Stop](https://docs.rs/trait.Stop.html)>(self, other: S) -> [StopAll](https://docs.rs/struct.StopAll.html)<Self, S>
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) { ... }
}## Expand description

Determines when the retry loop should stop.

Composition methods are provided directly on the trait with
`where Self: Sized` bounds, following the `Iterator` pattern.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::{RetryState, Stop};
struct StopAfterThree;
impl Stop for StopAfterThree {
    fn should_stop(&self, state: &RetryState) -> bool {
        const MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 3;
        state.attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS
    }
}
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Returns a strategy that stops when either side stops.

This is the named equivalent of the `|` operator. Both sides are
always evaluated (no short-circuit) so that stateful strategies
receive every `should_stop` call.

```
use relentless::{Stop, stop};
use core::time::Duration;
// These are equivalent:
let a = stop::attempts(5).or(stop::elapsed(Duration::from_secs(2)));
let b = stop::attempts(5) | stop::elapsed(Duration::from_secs(2));
```
Returns a strategy that stops only when both sides stop.

This is the named equivalent of the `&` operator. Both sides are
always evaluated (no short-circuit) so that stateful strategies
receive every `should_stop` call.

```
use relentless::{Stop, stop};
use core::time::Duration;
// These are equivalent:
let a = stop::attempts(5).and(stop::elapsed(Duration::from_secs(2)));
let b = stop::attempts(5) & stop::elapsed(Duration::from_secs(2));
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# relentless::predicate - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/predicate/index.html

## Expand description

Predicate trait and built-in retry predicate factories.

This module provides the [ Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html) trait and the default retry predicates:

- `any_error`- `Err`.
- `error`
- `result`- `Result<T, E>`.
- `ok`- `Ok`values and treats any- `Err`as terminal.

Predicates compose with `|` and `&` operators, or via `.or()` and `.and()`
methods on the [ Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html) trait.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAll.html)- All
- Composite predicate that retries only when **both**predicates retry.
- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAny.html)- Any
- Composite predicate that retries when **either**predicate retries.
- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateAnyError.html)- AnyError
- Predicate that retries on any error.
- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateError.html)- Error
- Predicate that retries when an `Err(e)`matches`matcher`.
- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateOk.html)- Ok
- Predicate that retries when an `Ok(value)`matches`matcher`.
- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateResult.html)- Result
- Predicate that retries based on the full `Result<T, E>`.
- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateUntil.html)- Until
- Predicate that negates the inner predicate’s decision.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/trait.Predicate.html)
- Examines the outcome of an operation and decides whether to retry.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [any_](https://docs.rs/fn.any_error.html)- error
- Creates a predicate that retries on any `Err`value.
- [error](https://docs.rs/fn.error.html)
- Produces a predicate that retries when `outcome`is`Err(e)`and`matcher(e)`returns`true`.
- [ok](https://docs.rs/fn.ok.html)
- Produces a predicate that retries when `outcome`is`Ok(value)`and`matcher(value)`returns`true`.
- [result](https://docs.rs/fn.result.html)
- Creates a predicate that retries when `matcher`returns`true`for the outcome.
- [until](https://docs.rs/fn.until.html)
- Wraps a predicate so that its `should_retry()`result is negated.

---

# relentless::prelude - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/prelude/index.html

## Expand description

Commonly used traits, glob-imported to enable the builder DSL.

The combinator methods (`.cap()`, `.full_jitter()`, `.chain()` on [ Wait](https://docs.rs/wait/trait.Wait.html);

`.or()`/`.and()` on [and](https://docs.rs/stop/trait.Stop.html)

`Stop`[) and the closure extensions (](https://docs.rs/predicate/trait.Predicate.html)

`Predicate``.retry()` on [,](https://docs.rs/trait.RetryExt.html)

`RetryExt``.retry_async()` on [) are trait methods, so the trait must be in scope to call them. Glob-import this module to bring them all in at once:](https://docs.rs/trait.AsyncRetryExt.html)

`AsyncRetryExt````
use relentless::prelude::*;
use relentless::wait;
use core::time::Duration;
// `.full_jitter()` and `.cap()` resolve without naming `Wait`.
let _ = wait::exponential(Duration::from_millis(100))
    .full_jitter()
    .cap(Duration::from_secs(5));
```
Strategy constructors (`wait::exponential`, `stop::attempts`, …) are *not*
re-exported here; import them explicitly by name.

## Expand description

# relentless::wait - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/wait/index.html

## Expand description

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Jittered](https://docs.rs/struct.Jittered.html)
- Applies jitter to an inner wait strategy’s output.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitCapped.html)- Capped
- Clamps an inner wait strategy’s output to a maximum duration.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitChain.html)- Chain
- A strategy that uses one wait strategy for the first `after`attempts, then switches to another.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitCombine.html)- Combine
- Composite strategy that returns the **sum**of two strategies’ outputs.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitExponential.html)- Exponential
- An exponentially increasing wait strategy.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitFixed.html)- Fixed
- A wait strategy that returns the same duration on every attempt.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitLinear.html)- Linear
- A linearly increasing wait strategy.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Wait](https://docs.rs/trait.Wait.html)
- Computes the delay duration between retry attempts.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decorrelated_](https://docs.rs/fn.decorrelated_jitter.html)- jitter
- Produces a decorrelated jitter strategy: each delay is random between `base`and three times the previous (post-clamp) delay.
- [exponential](https://docs.rs/fn.exponential.html)
- Produces an exponentially increasing strategy: `initial * 2^(n-1)`.
- [fixed](https://docs.rs/fn.fixed.html)
- Creates a wait strategy that waits a fixed duration between attempts.
- [linear](https://docs.rs/fn.linear.html)
- Creates a linearly increasing wait strategy.

# RetryStats in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/struct.RetryStats.html

```
pub struct RetryStats {
    pub attempts:
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub total_elapsed: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>,
    pub total_wait: [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html),
    pub stop_reason: [StopReason](https://docs.rs/enum.StopReason.html),
}## Expand description

Aggregate statistics for a completed retry execution.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::{RetryPolicy, RetryStats, stop, wait};
use core::time::Duration;
let policy = RetryPolicy::new()
    .stop(stop::attempts(3))
    .wait(wait::fixed(Duration::from_millis(5)));
let (_result, stats): (Result<(), _>, RetryStats) = policy
    .retry(|_| Err::<(), _>("fail"))
    .sleep(|_dur| {})
    .with_stats()
    .call();
assert_eq!(stats.attempts, 3);
assert_eq!(stats.total_wait, Duration::from_millis(10));
```
## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.attempts)

`attempts: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The total number of attempts executed.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.total_elapsed)

`total_elapsed: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>Total wall-clock elapsed time, or `None` when no clock is available.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.total_wait)

`total_wait: `[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)Cumulative duration requested from the wait strategy.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.stop_reason)

`stop_reason: `[StopReason](https://docs.rs/enum.StopReason.html)The reason the retry loop terminated.

# AttemptState in relentless - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/relentless/0.11.0/relentless/struct.AttemptState.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct AttemptState<'a, T, E> {
    pub attempt:
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub elapsed: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>,
    pub outcome: &'a [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, E>,
    pub next_delay: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>,
}## Expand description

Read-only context passed to the `after_attempt` hook.

This contains the attempt outcome plus timing/counting fields for the completed attempt.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use relentless::AttemptState;
use core::time::Duration;
fn log_attempt(state: &AttemptState<i32, String>) {
    println!("attempt {} result {:?}", state.attempt, state.outcome);
}
```
## Fields (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

## This struct is marked as non-exhaustive

`Struct { .. }` syntax; cannot be matched against without a wildcard `..`; and struct update syntax will not work.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.attempt)

`attempt: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The 1-indexed attempt number that just completed.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.elapsed)

`elapsed: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>Wall-clock time elapsed since the first attempt began.
`None` when no clock is available.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.outcome)

`outcome: &'a `[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, E>A reference to the outcome of the most recent attempt.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.next_delay)

`next_delay: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>The delay that will be applied before the next attempt, or `None`
if this is the terminal attempt (predicate accepted, stop condition
fired, or first-attempt success).
